newsitem.title: USA: Aluminium '97 supply balance seen tighter - Spector.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium '97 supply balance seen tighter - Spector.

text.p: The odds favor a tightening of the aluminium supply/demand balance in 1997, industry analyst Stewart Spector said in his monthly "Aluminium Service Industry" report.
"By the end of the year, almost all of the currently banked primary ingot capacity could be back in operation," Spector said.
"The only limitation on the smelters reaching capacity later this year could be the lack of availability of petroleum coke," he said.
LME three month aluminium was trading around $1627 a tonne in London Wednesday, after rallying since late 1996.
Last year primary ingot shipments were about 18.4 million tons, down about one percent from 1995, he said.
"However, end users de-stocked, so the real underlying consumption rate was probably up on the order of three to five percent from the year before," he said.
"If western world GDP in 1997 increases by a conservative 2.5 percent, then the underlying demand for aluminium could increase by at least the same amount, or 475,000 tons."
On a long term basis aluminium consumption has grown slightly faster than world GDP, he noted.
"In round numbers, last year demand exceeded supply by approximately 300,000 tons.

"This year we estimate maximum supply could reach 19.0 million tons, with an inventory draw of approximately 500,000 tons and shipments of 19.5 million tons. That eliminates all excess stocks, and reduces producers work-in-process stocks to less than the desired 1.9 months supply," he said.
